brief: Soft, performance-y everyday clothing for guys and gals who want to go from gym to coffee. Joggers around $90, shorts $65. Want to reach people who've already shown they spend on activewear.

profile.business_summary: DTC brand selling premium, soft, performance-y everyday clothing (such as joggers and shorts) designed to transition from the gym to casual settings, targeting activewear spenders.

relevant_tags.why: Everyday clothing designed for casual transitions like going to coffee.
Shoppers attending fitness classes are highly likely to buy activewear.
Yoga practitioners are a core demographic for performance-y everyday clothing.

persona_conflicts.conflict: Disinterested in luxury-only messaging or vague premium positioning; high price sensitivity.

note_signals.why: Fitness-engaged shoppers are the ideal target audience for activewear.
Users actively spending on self-care and fitness align perfectly with premium activewear buyers.
Conservative brand sensibility may clash with casual, gym-to-coffee activewear.
Comfort-seeking urban professionals are a strong demographic match for everyday performance wear.

profile.gate_reason: The product, price points, and target audience are clearly defined, allowing for immediate planning.

assumptions: Margin not given; assumed 60% (typical for apparel) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $90 x 60% x 1.3 orders = $70.20.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $1.80 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented. Guidance: at the assumed margin, a click is worth about $1.40; bidding above that loses money per customer. Set a target CPA or a lower max CPC to enforce it.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.
